content.text:
**Finding: compliant (at/near fallback).**

Section 14.1 is symmetric, carves M&A and asset sales out of the consent requirement for both parties, and there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right anywhere (Section 11 termination is limited to material breach and insolvency; no "deemed an assignment" language exists).

input.quote: 14.1 Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.
input.rationale: Section 14.1 is a mutual assignment clause that expressly permits Corio (our party) to assign without consent in connection with a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all related assets, so the walk-away risk (blanket prohibition with no M&A carve-out) is absent. Section 11 contains no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, and a document-wide search returns no "change of control" or deemed-assignment language, so a Corio change of control gives Commerce One no exit. This sits at the playbook fallback (mutual right to assign to successors; symmetric consent for other assignments). Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred position and are noted rather than flagged: there is no express affiliate carve-out for Corio, and the consent standard for other assignments is not qualified as "not to be unreasonably withheld." The direct-competitor consent proviso is symmetric and also protects Corio, so we would not disturb it.
